subject: Urgent: MedFlow live chat timeouts -> retry amplification / 5xx surge
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medflow.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live chat errors: spikes of 429/502, customers timing out

Hi Sean / Neha,

We started seeing a big spike this morning across our chat sessions — many requests are returning 429 or 502 during peak triage (09:00 - 09:30 PDT). Our client app is configured to retry on network errors and we've observed a wave of retries which appears to coincide with further backend errors. Customers are timing out in the middle of streams (client shows "connection lost") which kills the conversation state.

Attached is a short screen recording and a few pod logs. This is impacting diagnosis time for clinicians. We need an immediate mitigation and a short timeline for a permanent fix.

- Alex
Customer Success / MedFlow

Attachments: screenshot-429-burst.png (image/png), medflow-pod-logs-20270816.tar.gz (text/tar)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Live chat errors: spikes of 429/502, customers timing out

Neha / Marissa — forwarding the MedFlow report. They see 429/502 spikes and client retries are creating what looks like amplification. Rafael, can SRE start a triage? Priorities: 1) short-term patient impact mitigation, 2) root cause (is this backend saturation / routing?), 3) rollback/fallback plan.

Short notes from my quick look at the logs: 1) sudden per-client burst of repeated POSTs within 1-2s windows, 2) many KeepAlive disconnects at ~30s, 3) increased queued requests on the serving pool.

I can join an incident bridge. Neha, can you own the customer comms?

- Sean
Account Executive

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medflow.com>, ops@medflow.com (Priya Singh)
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat errors: spikes of 429/502, customers timing out

Alex / Priya — thanks for flagging and for the artifacts. We opened a P0 incident on our side and have SRE/infra on the bridge. Immediate next steps from our side:

- We are enabling client-side guidance: instruct MedFlow to increase client connect timeout to 45s and backoff jitter for retries (temporary, will update a carrier at the bottom).
- Rafael is running a rolling throttle to limit per-IP/session request rate to reduce amplification (will apply in 15m).
- Karthik is checking whether a model-variant fallback or lower-latency replica can be routed for your production traffic.

We will keep the bridge open and update every 15 minutes. I will send a short status note to you and your Operations lead after the first mitigation. Apologies — we know this is impacting clinicians.

- Neha
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Live chat errors: spikes of 429/502, customers timing out

Impact triage update:

- Applied per-session soft-throttle at the edge (limit: 6 reqs / 30s) to break retry storms. Initial metrics: 40% drop in 429 rate for affected LoadZone A.
- Increased stream keepalive probe to 45s for the affected pool to reduce premature idle disconnects.
- Identified a hot queue on serving-rack-9 caused by several long-running prefix-cache lookups; injecting additional workers on that rack to drain.

Next: collect 30m of post-mitigation telemetry, then evaluate whether an autoscale policy tweak (shorter scale-up cooldown) is required. Putting a watch on request backlog; will escalate to infra if backlog doesn't subside in 30m.

Rafael
SRE Lead

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medflow.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat errors: spikes of 429/502, customers timing out

Alex — quick update for your ops team: we've pushed a temporary config that does two things on your routed pool:

1) Soft per-session throttling (server-side) to prevent tight retry loops from burning capacity.
2) Lowered request timeouts on high-cost calls so we return fast-failure and avoid long blocking on the serving thread.

If you can increase client retry jitter + add exponential backoff on your SDK, that will avoid synchronized retries. We'll re-evaluate once Rafael's telemetry shows stable error rates.

Also sharing a short playbook (link below) that your mobile/web teams can apply for client changes to reduce impact quickly.

- Marissa
Customer Solutions

Related link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1N8q-MedFlow-MAP (MedFlow mitigation playbook)

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@medflow.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@medflow.com (Priya Singh), support@medflow.com (MedFlow Platform Team)
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat errors: spikes of 429/502, customers timing out

Thanks — big improvement after your edge throttle and the keepalive change. Error rate down ~65% and fewer disconnected sessions. A couple of notes:

- We still see occasional client timeouts when clinicians are on slow cellular. Could we explore a routing rule that sends mobile/low-bandwidth sessions to a lower-latency small-context model variant?
- Ops asked about a postmortem and whether this was due to autoscale cooldowns or an unexpected load pattern from our end (we rolled a feature yesterday that batches short prompts).

Happy to join a postmortem review — if you can share a time. Appreciate the rapid response.

- Alex
